# tgt   citation form: singular noun, infinitive verb, masculine
#       singular adjective, nominative singular for Latin/Old English.
# tgt2  plural for nouns, present participle for verbs. A blank tgt2 on
#       a noun means the English plural is never woven, which is the
#       correct outcome: weaving a singular target under an English
#       plural teaches a form that does not exist. iūsiūrandum's is blank
#       because no Classical text found has its plural: see
# ipa   the transcription of tgt, and ipa2 of tgt2: the tooltip prints a
#       row's under the form it wove, so virī is /ˈwɪriː/, not vir's /ˈwɪr/,
#       and amāns is stressed on its first syllable, where amāre is stressed
#       on its second. Both are written by tools/seed/fill_ipa.py. ipa2 is
#       last so that every reader of the first eight columns finds them
# Classical Latin, nominative singular and plural. English marks case by word
# order, so a nominative headword slots into an English clause unambiguously:
# "the rēx was angry" is clear where "the rēgis was angry" is wrong in both
# The etymon column is the English word descended from the Latin one, usually a
# learned borrowing. For Latin this is the whole point: the reader is not
# memorising a foreign word, they are being shown where their own word came
# from. "vaccine" from vacca, cow. "mile" from mīlle passūs. "peninsula" from
# So an etymon is a published claim, and it is held to a dictionary. The
# English word must have come from this Latin word, or from one built on it:
# a word built on the same root beside it is a cousin, and is not claimed —
# "ludicrous" is from "lūdere", not "lūdus". Every etymon names the entry it
# was checked against in tools/seed/la-etymons.tsv, and
# tests/tools/etymons.test.ts fails on one that names none.
# IPA is generated from the orthography, which is very nearly deterministic
# once vowel length is marked. Values are the standard classical
# The note column is a published sentence, so it is held to a dictionary.
# Every note names the entries it was checked against in
# tools/seed/la-notes.tsv, Lewis & Short for the Latin and etymonline for the
# English word it explains, and tests/tools/la-notes.test.ts fails on a note
# that names none, or that has been reworded since it was read.
# So is the gloss, the English word a row is woven for. Every row quotes the
# Lewis & Short entry that gives it in tools/seed/la-glosses.tsv, and
# tests/tools/la-glosses.test.ts fails on a row that quotes none, or a quote
# holding neither the English word nor a word named to stand for it.
